observed: The yim20 standard deviations (19.4 µm, 2.8 nm, 0.0003 nm) were facts of quantity other; what they spread, and between what, lived only in the statement. Q5 and Q25 matched them by label words, so the 2.8 nm plateau sd was also used for the outside thickness.
root_cause: The schema had no way to say that a value is a spread of another quantity: no statistic, no 'between what' and no n. Spread facts were typed like any measured value of quantity other.
fix: lists.QUALIFIERS gains stat (sd, relative_sd, half_range, tolerance, minimum, maximum), between (runs, pieces, position, repeat_measurement, items) and n (a number or not_stated). Each instance names the quantity it spreads: PD50, slope and plateau thickness sd between 4 runs on the replicate comparison; the chip height tolerance between items; the wafer thickness relative sd between positions; the calibration temperature half-range between runs, under a new recipe measurement activity (the calibration runs measured the reactor). Its condition is its parent. check.py: a stat fact must carry between and n, and only a stat fact may give an observation a setting quantity. query.spread reads the spread fact by quantity key (spread_key), not by label.
verified: verified: the 8 facts carry quantity, stat, between and n; no other stat fact exists; check.py passes; Q5 now computes the outside-thickness sd over the 4 members instead of borrowing the plateau sd

observed: The uncertainty column held 49 numbers of different kinds without saying which: the spread between the two NPCs of a gre23 run, Rietveld fit errors, the electrode-area uncertainty of ρ, the measurement uncertainty of ȳ, literature averages, caliper and weighing values; six mat22 entries read '0.1.'.
root_cause: fill_uncertainty parsed the number after ± with [\d.]+, which swallows a sentence-final period, and stored only the number: the kind of ± the paper states (in a caption or a sentence) had no column.
fix: facts.FIELDS gains uncertainty_kind (lists.UNCERTAINTY_KINDS: pieces, runs, position, repeat_measurement, fit, measurement, literature, propagated, not_stated) and uncertainty_n; facts.uncertainty_kinds sets them per paper from what the paper says (gre23: mass gain and GPC ± are the spread within a run's NPC pair, n 2; Table II wt% and size are pattern-fit errors; ρ is the electrode-area uncertainty; ȳ a measurement uncertainty; the AR ± propagated from L; mat22: literature averages, the wafer map over positions; Table 1 and the remaining gre23 values do not say: not_stated). The parser takes a number, not a run of digits and periods. check.py requires a kind on every uncertainty and a numeric uncertainty. Q25 reads the kind, not the word 'spread'.
verified: verified: 49 of 49 carry a kind (gre23 pieces 6, fit 8, measurement 6, propagated 1, not_stated 10; mat22 not_stated 15, literature 2, position 1); no uncertainty fails the number check; for 25 of them the paper does not state the kind (not_stated)

observed: The Series F card said 'within reproducibility': it divided the range of three runs by one sd measured over the replicate set (samples 2, 4, 8, 12) at another condition, and said neither. Series A, three samples of one run, was judged against run-to-run scatter.
root_cause: The page computed its own reproducibility set in JavaScript (reproOf) and compared max − min with 1 sd; nothing knew what varies between the members (runs or pieces of one run) or between the repeats, or where the repeats were made.
fix: query.judge(T, comparison, result key): what varies between the members (member_kind: runs, pieces of one run, model runs); noise only of the same kind (a stat=sd spread fact with between= that kind, else the sd over a stated replicate comparison of that kind); the range of the n member values against d2(n) × sd; one plain sentence naming the base condition ('smaller than the scatter between runs at the base condition (4 runs, sd 19 µm)'), or 'no repeated runs; the size of the difference cannot be judged'. The comparison card shows judge() from the build; the JavaScript reproducibility set is no longer used. Q5 composes judge().
verified: verified: Series F PD50 range 13 µm against 33 µm expected from 3 runs (smaller); Series A (one run) cannot be judged; Series B–E judged against runs; sims are model runs; every mat22 comparison and gre23's schedules: no repeated runs, cannot be judged; the page no longer says 'within reproducibility'
